research_mode: official UK government and ONS primary statistical publications and methodology only; every claim carries a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, candidate value, local risk score or business result claimed

sources.name: Official-statistics status
verified_claims: Police use of force statistics are classified as official statistics.
limitations: Official-statistics status does not remove the documented recording and interpretation limitations.

sources.name: Development-label removal
verified_claims: The former experimental or official-statistics-in-development label was removed from the year ending March 2021 series.
limitations: The label change does not make force-level reporting perfectly comparable.

sources.name: National recording requirement
verified_claims: Police forces have been required to record the specified use-of-force data since April 2017.
limitations: The requirement does not guarantee every report is complete or consistently interpreted.

sources.name: Annual Data Requirement collection
verified_claims: Forces submit use-of-force data to the Home Office through the Annual Data Requirement.
limitations: ADR submission is an administrative collection and not an independently observed event register.

sources.name: Force coverage
verified_claims: The collection covers the 43 Home Office police forces and, voluntarily from the year ending March 2024, British Transport Police.
limitations: Coverage does not make local force systems or validation practices identical.

sources.name: Report counting unit
verified_claims: One report represents one officer's use of force on one person.
limitations: A single incident can generate several reports when several officers use force.

sources.name: Multiple tactics per report
verified_claims: One report can include multiple tactics, reasons, impact factors, locations and outcomes.
limitations: Fields within one report must not be interpreted as one-to-one causal links.

sources.name: Captured report fields
verified_claims: Reports capture tactics, reasons, person characteristics, injuries, outcomes and location type.
limitations: The fields are officer-recorded and can contain missing or contradictory values.

sources.name: Designated public-order exclusion
verified_claims: The national collection excludes force used at designated public-order events where detailed individual reporting is not feasible.
limitations: The dataset is not a complete inventory of all force used by police.

sources.name: Local recording systems
verified_claims: Police forces choose their own systems for recording use-of-force data.
limitations: System differences can affect question wording, validation and field completeness.

sources.name: Officer-judgement dependence
verified_claims: Use-of-force reporting remains partly dependent on the reporting officer's judgement and interpretation.
limitations: Different officers at the same incident may record person or outcome details differently.

sources.name: Completeness quality assurance
verified_claims: Home Office quality assurance checks whether submitted data are complete.
limitations: A completeness check cannot prove that every use of force was reported.

sources.name: Contradiction quality assurance
verified_claims: Home Office analysts query missing or contradictory values and work with forces on corrections.
limitations: Corrected administrative data can still contain residual error.

sources.name: Multiple-officer reporting
verified_claims: Each officer who uses force on an individual must complete a separate report for that person.
limitations: Report totals are not counts of unique people or unique incidents.

sources.name: Tactic-outcome linkage boundary
verified_claims: The collection cannot directly link an individual tactic to a reason, outcome, location or injury where multiple values are recorded.
limitations: A hospitalisation or injury field must not be attributed to a specific tactic without separate evidence.

sources.name: Injury-causality boundary
verified_claims: Reported injuries or hospitalisation may pre-date or be unrelated to the officer's use of force.
limitations: Injury records are not medical causation findings.

sources.name: Multiple-location boundary
verified_claims: A report may cover force used in more than one location.
limitations: A location category cannot establish where each tactic occurred or identify a parcel.

sources.name: Specific-person and event limitation
verified_claims: The national data cannot reliably provide details of a specific person or event.
limitations: The collection must not be used for exact-address attribution or individual prediction.

sources.name: Rounding methodology
verified_claims: Counts are published unrounded and percentages use stated rounding rules.
limitations: Unrounded administrative counts still contain the inaccuracies inherent in large recording systems.

sources.name: Revision policy
verified_claims: The latest Home Office publication incorporates revisions to previous data under its revisions policy.
limitations: Values should be versioned by release date and may change after force resubmission.
